abstract:
Service rejection is common in the service sector and a routine part of commercial interactions. As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into service delivery, it is important to understand how AI-driven rejections affect customer satisfaction compared with rejections made by human agents. This research shows that consumers are generally less satisfied when an AI agent, rather than a human agent, rejects their applications. This is because consumers are more likely to assign greater blame to AI agents, perceiving them as having lower decision-making ability. We also examine how explanations shape consumer responses to AI-driven rejections. Our findings indicate that providing a teleological explanation, clarifying
                    why
                    a rejection occurred, effectively mitigates negative reactions compared with providing a mechanistic explanation, which clarifies
                    how
                    the rejection was made, or providing no explanation at all. This research contributes to the ongoing discussions about consumer responses to AI-based decisions, particularly when those decisions deliver unfavorable outcomes.

ur.ai_reason: 消费者实验检验AI拒绝及解释对满意度影响
ur.tldr: 比较AI与人工拒绝服务申请对满意度的影响后发现，消费者对AI拒绝更不满，并因其决策能力 perceived 较低而归责更多。目的论解释说明拒绝原因，比机制论解释或无解释更能缓解负面反应。

title: When AI Says No: AI-Driven Service Rejection and Its Impact on Customer Satisfaction
title_zh: 当AI说“不”：AI驱动的服务拒绝对客户满意度的影响
